'''Ina Koch''' (born 1958) is a German [[bioinformatics]] researcher who holds the Chair of Molecular Bioinformatics at [[Goethe University Frankfurt]], in the faculty of mathematics and computer science.{{r|mbi}} She has published research on the use of [[maximum common subgraph]]s and [[Petri net]]s to model problems in biology, and on the prediction of [[Genetic purging|deleterious alleles]].

==Education and career==
Koch was born in 1958 in East [[Berlin]], and studied quantum chemistry at [[Leipzig University]], working there with {{ill|Cornelius Weiss|de}}. She became a researcher in the Institute for Cybernetics and Information Processing of the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin]], and after the German reunification in 1990, became a researcher for the {{ill|GMD-Forschungszentrum Informationstechnik|de}} from 1992 to 1996, and completed a doctorate in theoretical computer science.{{r|cef}}

After postdoctoral research with [[Jens Reich]] at the [[Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine in the Helmholtz Association]], and with [[Martin Vingron]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Molecular Genetics]], she took a professorship in 2002 at the [[Berliner Hochschule für Technik|Berlin University of Applied Sciences and Technology]]. She moved in 2005 to the [[University of Jena]], and again in 2010 to her present position in Frankfurt.{{r|cef}}
